knowledge:
- key_parameters:
    - eset: An ExpressionSet object containing the gene expression data.
    - T: The cycle period of the periodic process (e.g., T.yeast <- 85).
    - times: A numeric vector specifying the times of measurement (e.g., pData(yeast)$time).
    - background.model: The model used to generate background data; "rr" for random permutation or "ar1" for autoregressive AR(1) model.
    - N: The number of background datasets to generate (e.g., N=100 or N=1000).
    - progress: Logical value (TRUE/FALSE) to enable or disable a progress bar during FDR calculation.
    - thres: Threshold for the fraction of missing values allowed per gene (e.g., thres=0.25).
    - mode: Imputation method for missing values; "mean" for average value, or "knn"/"wknn" for (weighted) k-nearest neighbors.
- alternatives:
    - For background models, "rr" (random permutation) and Gaussian models are alternatives to "ar1", but they neglect autocorrelation and tend to overestimate the number of periodic genes. "ar1" is preferred for accurate significance testing.
    - For missing value imputation, "knn" or "wknn" are recommended alternatives to "mean" as they perform better, though they are more computationally intensive.
- when_to_use:
    - Use this package when analyzing time-series transcriptomic datasets (such as microarray data) to identify genes associated with periodic biological processes (e.g., cell cycle, circadian rhythm) while controlling for false discovery rates.
- pitfalls:
    - Neglecting autocorrelation by using randomized background models ("rr") can lead to a substantial overestimation of significantly periodic genes.
    - Fourier score calculations do not tolerate missing values; genes with excessive missing values must be filtered out, and remaining NAs must be imputed before analysis.
    - The fdrfourier function evaluates only the expression matrix and ignores phenoData ordering; the columns of the expression matrix must be ordered chronologically.
    - Replicated arrays in the expression matrix are treated as independent; they should be averaged prior to analysis or split into separate ExpressionSet objects.
    - Calculating FDRs using empirical background distributions for large datasets or large N can be computationally expensive and take up to several days.

workflows.name: periodic_expression_analysis
workflows.intent: Assess the statistical significance of periodic gene expression in time-series data using Fourier analysis and AR(1) or random permutation background models.
input: ExpressionSet (containing time-series gene expression data and associated time-point metadata)
workflows.stages:
1. Filter out genes with excessive missing values using filter.NA.
2. Impute remaining missing values using fill.NA.
3. Standardize the expression values (mean of zero, standard deviation of one) using standardise.
4. Extract measurement times and define the cycle period.
5. Calculate false discovery rates (FDR) using fdrfourier with "rr" and "ar1" background models.
6. Identify significantly periodic genes by filtering on the calculated FDR.
workflows.code:
library(cycle) 
set.seed(1)
data(yeast)
yeast <- yeast[1:200,]
yeast <- filter.NA(yeast, thres=0.25)
yeast <- fill.NA(yeast,mode="mean")
yeast <- standardise(yeast)
auto.corr <- 0
for (i in 2:dim(exprs(yeast))[[2]]){
 auto.corr[i] <- cor(exprs(yeast)[,i-1],exprs(yeast)[,i])
 }
auto.corr 
T.yeast <- 85  
times.yeast <-  pData(yeast)$time 
times.yeast
NN <- 100 
fdr.rr <- fdrfourier(eset=yeast,T=T.yeast,times=times.yeast,background.model="rr",N=NN,progress=FALSE)
fdr.ar1 <- fdrfourier(eset=yeast,T=T.yeast,times=times.yeast,background.model="ar1",N=NN,progress=FALSE)
sum(fdr.rr$fdr < 0.25) 
sum(fdr.ar1$fdr < 0.25)
fdr.ar1$fdr[which(fdr.ar1$fdr < 0.25)]
